name: Blood and soil
summary: Blood and soil (Blut und Boden) is the idea that a people defined by hereditary blood is bound to the land it works, with the free peasant farm as the source of the nation's life. Popularised by Richard Walther Darre, it called for a new hereditary elite, eugenic marriage rules, inherited family farms and a turn away from industry, cities, liberalism and Marxism. It became the motto of Nazi Germany's agrarian estate and the basis of the 1933 Hereditary Farm Law.
scope: The blood and soil doctrine as set out by Darre in A New Nobility of Blood and Soil (1930), as described in Bramwell's biography, and as put into practice in the Hereditary Farm Law of 1933 and the Reichsnaehrstand. It does not cover Nazism as a whole, Hitler's other policies, other uses of the phrase (Zionist, white nationalist) or the Artaman League beyond Darre's own writings.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Darre wants a new hereditary nobility with institutions that retain blood of proven value in the hereditary line, the opposite of abolishing hereditary rank.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Darre says Marxism ignores how values come into being and explains history by blood, breeding and the hereditary quality of leadership classes, not class conflict.

collective-farming.rationale: The Hereditary Farm Law places the farm in the possession of 'free peasants' as family property, and Darre calls Marxism and a Germanic peasantry 'irreconcilable mortal enemies'.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Bramwell reports Darre rejected the power-politics ideal of a Germany ruling the splintered nations of the North, which Edgar Jung had urged.

democracy-best.rationale: Darre argues that democracies, by refusing to recognise hereditary inequality, lose their ancestral talents and die culturally after a short flowering, and Bramwell calls him strongly anti-democratic.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Darre warns that nature punishes the mixing of different stocks so that the higher is depressed by the lower, and praises Germanic nobility that let no foreign blood into its families.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Darre holds that the owner of land has a 'blood duty' to his race and people, which liberalism's right of the owner to his land does not recognise.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Hereditary Farm Law of 1933 limited the status of peasant to citizens 'of German or kindred blood', and Bramwell reports a descent test back to 1800, so rights over inherited land were not equal before the law.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Its record, the Hereditary Farm Law and the Reichsnaehrstand, tied the peasant estate that was the 'blood-source of the German people' to German or kindred blood.

free-trade.rationale: Bramwell reports Darre's plan for the peasant state needed an autarkic trade structure to protect farmers from competitive capitalist food production and from manipulators of world commodity markets.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Darre holds that natural science confirms the hereditary inequality of humans and speaks of a person's genetic or 'racial value', treating the Nordic race as the stock to be preserved.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: His marriage-law scheme proposes institutions that inhibit the multiplication of the 'inferior' and permits marriage of one hereditary class of women only if sterilisation guarantees childlessness.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The German Historical Institute's account says the blood and soil ideology propounded a general turning away from industry toward an agrarian economy, and Bramwell reports Darre proposing to de-industrialise Germany and let the cities decay, though neither calls industrial civilisation a disaster in those words.

land-value-tax.rationale: Darre dismisses Henry George's rent theory as economic nonsense and ties land to a family and blood duty, so a land-rent tax replacing other taxes contradicts his position.

limit-population.rationale: Bramwell reports Darre called population control 'a castration morality' and preferred resettlement.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The law's stated aim was to shield farms from the vagaries of the market economy, and its subsistence-acre definition sets a farm apart from market conditions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He rejects 'purely material thinking' in Marxism and Liberalism and holds that hereditary and racial value conditions a people's fate.

national-rebirth.rationale: The New Nobility proposes renewing a German people said to have lost a healthy leadership, by breeding and settlement on hereditary farms.

natural-rulers.rationale: Darre's New Nobility argues for a leadership class bred and selected for hereditary value, grounded in the 'recognized hereditary inequality of humanity'.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Darre calls Liberalism and Marxism two sides of the same materialist thinking and holds that both disregard the people's way of life and blood.

organic-representation.rationale: His Hegehof plan, as Bramwell reports it, divided society into corporations each forming a self-governing chamber, with only farmers from a Hegehof holding a vote.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bramwell quotes Darre's 1920s letter founding a party on 'unceasing struggle against all Jewry and Parliamentarianism', and describes him as strongly anti-democratic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The law's preamble says it preserves the peasantry through the 'ancient German method of inheritance'.

property-fundamental.rationale: The law took away the owner's freedom to sell, mortgage or divide a hereditary farm, so ownership could be overridden for the people's sake.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The law ties the inherited farm to the purpose of preserving the peasantry as the blood-source of the people, and forbids selling or mortgaging it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Darre's programme looks back to a Germanic order of peasant inheritance and nobility, and the German History documents call it reactionary agrarianism, a return from industry to the land.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Bramwell reports that the Blood and Soil school saw peasant farming as morally superior, embodying frugality, loyalty and hard work, and Darre's Nordic ideal rejected urban life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Bramwell reports Darre urged resettlement of Germany's former lands in the Baltic and Poland as the obvious outlet instead of population control, but wanted no expansion beyond German or formerly German territory.

traditional-family.rationale: Darre derives the peasant's bond to land from the Germanic conception of family and treats the peasant family as the carrier of the basic life ideas of the people.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The law's preamble says many prosperous small and medium farms spread across the country are the best guarantee for a vigorous people, though the law also protects holdings up to 125 hectares and was not used to break up large estates.

notes: Themes searched: economy, government, society, ecology, world, liberty, culture. Darre's 1930 book is read in a 2021 translation by a political publisher; its passages are cited as paraphrase and were not checked against the German original. Large parts of the statement bank (health care, welfare, civil liberties, foreign policy, technology) are not addressed by Darre, Bramwell or the law, so they stay null.
